options: A permanent custom field added to the object
A report-only field that groups values of another field into categories you define
A dashboard filter for viewers
A type of joined-report block
questions.explain: A bucket column lives only inside the report and groups the values of a source field into named categories.

questions.q: Which T-SQL construct is closest to a bucket column?
options: A CASE expression
A cursor
A foreign key
A stored procedure
questions.explain: A bucket maps values or ranges to labels, which is exactly what CASE WHEN ... THEN ... does.

questions.q: Which of these is a good use for bucketing?
options: Permanently renaming a picklist value in the org
Changing who owns a record
Grouping opportunity Amount into Small, Medium, and Large bands
Deleting duplicate accounts
questions.explain: Turning a high-cardinality numeric field into a few readable bands is the classic case for bucketing.

questions.q: Five different reports all need the same Small/Medium/Large deal-size categories. What is usually the better approach?
options: Build a separate bucket in each of the five reports and keep them in sync by hand
Use a joined report for all five
Rename the reports so they match
Ask an admin for a formula field on the object so it is defined once
questions.explain: Bucket fields belong to one report. A formula field on the object is defined once and can be used across reports and dashboards.

questions.q: After building a bucket, the report shows an unexpected group named "Other" or a blank group. What most likely happened?
options: Some source values were not assigned to any bucket
The report type was deleted
Bucket fields cannot be grouped
The report switched to Tabular format
questions.explain: Unassigned values usually fall into a blank or Other group. Scan for it and assign the missing values to a bucket.
